result:
Good, this is the only `*AgentTest` in the project, so the full suite run matches. The test file is complete and self-contained at `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinterAgentTest.java`.

## Summary

Created `CSVPrinterAgentTest` (30 tests) covering construction/validation, `print`/`println`/`printComment`/`printRecord`/`printRecords` (including `ResultSet` overloads via a real H2 in-memory DB), quoting, `close`/`flush` delegation, and record counting.

Two tests fail, and each reveals a real bug in `CSVPrinter`, not a test error:

1. **`testRecordCountExcludesHeaderRecord`** — `getRecordCount()`'s Javadoc states the count "does not include ... headers," but the constructor prints the header via `printRecord(...)`, which calls `endOfRecord()` and increments `recordCount`. So right after construction with a header, `getRecordCount()` returns `1` instead of the documented `0`.

2. **`testPrintRecordsFlatIterablePrintsSingleRecord`** — `printRecords(Iterable<?>)`'s Javadoc says a flat iterable of simple objects ("If the given Iterable only contains simple objects, this method will print a single record like `printRecord(Iterable)`") should be printed as **one** record. Instead, `printRecordObject` falls through to `printRecord(value)` for each element individually, so `printRecords(Arrays.asList("a","b","c"))` prints three separate one-value records (`a\r\nb\r\nc\r\n`) instead of one record (`a,b,c\r\n`).
